listing.name: Chris Sawyer's Locomotion / OpenLoco (OpenLoco)
listing.summary: Explore Chris Sawyer's Locomotion / OpenLoco (OpenLoco) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Start the game
steps.instruction: On first Play, OpenLoco detects your installed Chris Sawyer’s Locomotion files or asks you to select the original folder containing Data/g1.DAT. The official portable engine needs no separate build or installer.

references.title: Set up OpenLoco on Linux
references.instruction: Use the official x86-64 AppImage. The reviewed player needs glibc 2.28 or newer. Make it executable and run it directly to select your installed Locomotion directory containing Data/g1.DAT. Preserve the whole profile under ~/.config/OpenLoco or the actual XDG_CONFIG_HOME location. Keep separately selected saves, landscapes, custom objects and original-game folders.

references.title: Set up OpenLoco on Apple Silicon
references.instruction: Use the upstream macos-arm64 ZIP. If downloading through Portcove, clear “Extract the archive after downloading”. Extract it with the system archive tool and keep the entire OpenLoco.app bundle. Upstream describes this build as unsigned and unnotarized. Follow its Mac instructions if Gatekeeper blocks it. Start it directly, select the Locomotion directory containing Data/g1.DAT and preserve ~/Library/Application Support/OpenLoco and custom locations. You manage this external copy and its updates.

presentation.manual_preparation: On first Play, OpenLoco detects your installed Chris Sawyer’s Locomotion files or asks you to select the original folder containing Data/g1.DAT. The official portable engine needs no separate build or installer. OpenLoco normally keeps settings, saves, autosaves, custom objects, landscapes, screenshots and crashes under AppData/OpenLoco, outside Portcove backups. Its original Locomotion folder stays external. The runtime’s data folder contains version-owned engine assets, not a generic player-data folder; no in-folder persistence is declared. Existing external installations keep their files and runtime update owner. Gameplay, platform minimums and packaged Desktop acceptance remain separate observations.
